newsitem.title: FINLAND: Outokumpu warns of weaker 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Outokumpu warns of weaker 1996 profits.

text.p: Finnish metals and mining group Outokumpu Oy said in a statement on Monday its May-August result would be clearly weaker than in January-April and that its 1996 result would be significantly weaker than in 1995.

It cited a 150 million markka copper products inventory loss, declining prices of stainless steel and copper and said it would write down its mine property by 150 million markka in the May-August due to a down-scaling of its Forrestania nickel mine in Australia.

Outokumpu posted a 305 million markka profit before extraordinary items in January-April, down from 789 million a year earlier. Its full-year 1995 profit before extraordinary items was 1.48 billion markka.
"The result of the Outokumpu Group for the second tertial of the year will be clearly weaker than for the fist tertial," Outokumpu said.

"Although the financial development is expected to improve somewhat during the rest of the year, the Group's result for the whole of 1996 will, in the light of the current outlook, be significantly weaker than the previous year," it said.
Outokumpu blamed much of the sharp fall in its January-April profits on weak stainless steel prices and now said stainless steel prices had continued to decline since April.
"At the moment, market prices in Europe are some 40 percent below the peak level of early 1995 and nearly 20 percent below the average price of the first tertial of this year," it said.
"However, (stainless steel) demand has picked up since the early part of the year and prices are expected to improve somewhat during the rest of the year," it added.
Outokumpu said copper prices had fallen 25 percent in May-June to $0.90/lb but added that most of its 1996-1997 copper mine production was hedged with forwards and options.
"At the end of August, the company had open copper forward contracts for 34,600 tonnes averaging $1.13/lb and copper put option contracts for 20,000 tonnes with average strike price of $0.95/lb.
The May-August result of Outokumpu's Copper Products business will be hit by an inventory loss of about 150 million markka caused by declining copper prices, the company said.

"Based on additional studies completed in August, the ore reserves of the Forrestania nickel mine in Australia have been further down-scaled ... a 150 million markka write-down on mine property will be done in the second tertial financial accounts," Outokumpu said.
The group's January-August results will be released on October 7.
